## Working Read

This essay closes the ordinary escape route of externality. Families can transfer cost to communities, communities to populations or landscapes, and markets to future periods; Earth remains the materially coupled field that carries the consequence.

The essay does not ask for human purity or infinite restraint. It asks for widened boundaries, honest feedback, and a civilization whose positive loops create renewal rather than treating planetary substrate as an invisible reserve.

## Core Claim

Earth can remain a shared inheritance only when human systems internalize the material costs they have been relocating; there is no elsewhere outside the planetary account.

## Key Ideas

- Earth is not a backdrop but the coupled substrate of every human loop.
- A planetary boundary is a range of viable conditions, not merely a wall.
- Positive and negative loops describe system dynamics, not moral categories.
- Delayed feedback makes planetary depletion appear mysterious until thresholds are crossed.
- Planetary standing cannot depend on purchasing power.
- Sustainability requires regeneration and repair, not restraint alone.

## Cost Series

Earth is the planetary scale of the Cost series: [Self](../the-cost-of-self/index.md) → [Family](../the-cost-of-family/index.md) → [Community](../the-cost-of-community/index.md) → [Earth](../the-cost-of-earth/index.md) → [Cosmos](../the-cost-of-cosmos/index.md).

## Open Questions

- What would it mean to make planetary externalities legible before delayed feedback becomes irreversible?
- Which forms of standing must be extended beyond human purchasing power?
- How can Earth civilization build positive loops of renewal rather than organizing only around restraint?
- What does consent mean when the affected system cannot answer in human language?
